reviews.title: A Wonderful App for Keeping Your Home Running Smoothly!
reviews.text:
I absolutely love Sweepy! It’s so much more than a cleaning app. It’s a wonderful way to organize, manage, and keep track of all the daily, weekly, monthly, and seasonal responsibilities that come with maintaining a home.

One of the things I appreciate most is being able to keep track of those household tasks that are so easy to forget or overlook. I would especially love to see a monthly household maintenance chart that includes things beyond everyday cleaning.

Living in Florida, there are so many additional things to remember to keep a home running properly, such as changing AC filters, cleaning AC vents, checking air conditioning systems, inspecting for moisture and mold, checking for pests, cleaning dryer vents, maintaining appliances, and keeping an eye on things that Florida’s heat and humidity can affect.

These aren’t necessarily everyday chores, but they are important responsibilities that help protect our homes and prevent costly repairs.

Sweepy makes managing a household feel less overwhelming because it helps take the guesswork out of remembering what needs to be done and when.

I think a household maintenance section, especially one that could be customized for different climates like Florida, would make an already great app even better!

Thank you for creating such a helpful app. It’s wonderful to have a little help keeping everything in order!

reviews.title: Perfect for an ADHD brain
reviews.text:
I absolutely love Sweepy! I’ve tried different ways of keeping up with housework, but this is one of the few apps that actually helps my brain feel less overwhelmed instead of giving me another thing to manage.

I especially love how customizable everything is. You can rate tasks from low to high effort, completely customize how often each task repeats, organize everything by room, and even have different people in the household use it. I can actually see everything that needs to be done without having to keep the entire house running in my head. 😂

I have ADHD, and being able to get all of those little tasks out of my brain and into one organized place genuinely helps my brain rest. I pay annually, and I think the price is very reasonable for how much I use it. Definitely worth it for me! ❤️

reviews.title: Pretty Glitchy
reviews.text:
Overall, I find the Sweepy app really helpful. It does a great job of helping me stay on top of household chores and keeps me from letting things pile up or get forgotten. However, the app is extremely glitchy and definitely needs some improvement.

The biggest issue I’ve encountered is the profile photo. I have tried many, many times to upload one, using different photos and file types, and it fails every single time. At this point, it doesn’t seem like a problem with the photo—it seems like the upload feature simply isn’t working.

I was also really excited about the gamification mode because I thought it would be a fun way to use the points I earn. Unfortunately, that feature doesn’t seem to work either. You can spend your points to purchase items, but the items don’t actually appear in your room, so there’s no way to see or use what you’ve purchased. I’m honestly not sure what the intended functionality is supposed to be, but right now it feels unfinished or broken.

I really like the concept of Sweepy and find the core chore-tracking features genuinely useful, but these glitches make the overall experience frustrating. How are issues like the profile photo upload and the gamification functionality not being caught and fixed? These features clearly need someone to take a closer look.

reviews.title: Has potential if you need gamification to motivate
reviews.text:
I was recommended this app for my ADHD tendencies.  Because I find it hard to motivate myself to action due to overwhelm, decision paralysis, etc.,—and I love those home design games—I thought this would be the perfect app for me to help me with my home upkeep and cleaning.  I decided to spend the money to buy a year’s subscription ($20 is not so bad).  

I have been using the app for a couple of months.  The UI to set up tasks is fairly easy—although it’s a lot to add your cleaning routine set up in all one go.  

It does help me get some tasks done—as a reminder and a physical touch to check it off the list—but…

My problem with this app is that the gamification UI is simple—I feel like I am looking at a slightly better Minecraft for the home design set up. The room elements are pixelated—can we upgrade the game look to this century?? 

Placement of those items are also very rigid—and small.  Some pictures are the size of a postage stamp in relation to the room—can I even tell what the picture is? Nope.  

Some elements you can’t place if you don’t have the room in your setup.  I live in an apartment—no garage—so please don’t show me items in the Market tab that I can’t place! And who has a dressing room? I don’t, but some items that are used in the dressing room could be used in my bedroom.  Why not be more flexible? 

One last thing—I would love to be able to look at my rooms in a carousel UI so I can tell what they look like without having to tap into the room’s list and the out to the next room. (If you’re able to do that, it’s not intuitive.)

This app has potential  (so being generous with 3 stars) but at this moment, if I was at a point to renew my subscription, I wouldn’t.  And 10 months from now with no major updates, I probably won’t then too.

I also wish you could link tasks that you frequently do together. For example, I’m never going to just vacuum one room so I wish I could link vacuuming all the rooms upstairs and all of the rooms downstairs. The app is definitely worth the cost. Just could use a few tweaks in my opinion.

I like the feature where I can schedule a task for a certain day of the week. I would also like to schedule a task for a certain day of the month. reviews.title: Best ADHD-Friendly Cleaning App
reviews.text:
I can’t rate this app highly enough. If you have ADHD, you’ve probably spent a lot of time looking at apps to help manage it. And you’ve probably noticed most of them are useless with extremely predatory subscription models. Sweepy is different! It’s a rare *truly free* app in the age of every app costing $9.99 a month after you forget to cancel the first week free trial. There is a Sweepy pro tier, but you can use all the most important features without it. 

It took me a while to set up my chores in a way that made sense to me. Instead of splitting them up by room, I split them up by frequency. So I have a “room” for weekly cleans, a “room” for monthly cleans, etc. And I did realize I needed to break every little step into its own chore for my brain to not be overwhelmed. So there’s not a chore to “dust the living room”but a chore to “dust the tv,” “dust the bookshelves,” “dust the coffee table,” etc. That way I can see every step of every clean in the house visually. 

Once I figured out a setup that worked for me, it’s been an actual game changer! My house has never stayed *consistently* clean before.

I guess I didn’t realize I was overwhelming myself by not mentally breaking down chores enough - I might go weeks without cleaning the sink because I didn’t have time to also clean the counter, that kind of thing. And I just wasn’t able to keep track of all the little things that needed doing unless I did them all at the same time. 

Anyway, I can’t recommend Sweeply enough. It’s a rare actually helpful, useful, and FREE app.

reviews.title: Sweepy App Review: A Clever but Unnecessary Complexity
reviews.text:
Sweepy is a well-designed and innovative cleaning companion that turns household chores into a structured, gamified experience. For just $2.99 per month or $19.99 per year, users can create schedules, assign tasks, and track their progress across different rooms in their home. It’s an app that brings clarity and organization to cleaning routines, helping users break down tasks into manageable steps.

At its core, Sweepy excels in providing guidance, especially for those who struggle with maintaining a cleaning schedule. It ensures that no area is overlooked and encourages consistency through its gamification mechanics. The app offers clear instructions on what needs to be done in each room, making it a useful tool for those who feel overwhelmed by household maintenance.

However, Sweepy also highlights an ironic contradiction—by simplifying cleaning, it arguably makes it more complicated. Cleaning is fundamentally straightforward: put things in order, wipe down surfaces, and remove visible dirt. The process doesn’t require extensive planning, tracking, or digital intervention. Instead of immediately tackling a messy space, users might find themselves spending more time inputting tasks, checking progress, and engaging with the app rather than just getting the work done.

For individuals who genuinely need structured motivation, Sweepy is a fantastic app. But for those who prefer a direct approach to tidying up, it risks turning an inherently simple task into an unnecessarily complex routine. While the app is undeniably well-made, its very existence raises the question: do we really need a tool to tell us how to clean, or should we just get up and do it?

Many people turn to apps like Sweepy because they feel overwhelmed by household tasks and need help structuring their cleaning routines. Unfortunately, the free version offers little beyond what you could accomplish with a simple to-do list on paper. What’s intriguing is that the app claims to reduce overwhelm by assigning manageable daily tasks. However, I wasn’t able to properly evaluate that claim because three days simply isn’t enough time to see how it affects long-term habits.

In contrast, TODY offers a 30-day free trial which allowed me to experience its full capabilities over a meaningful period. 

The value lies in how well they integrate into everyday life and help build lasting habits. Sweepy could be great, but to truly showcase its effectiveness, it needs a more generous trial period. If users can’t properly test whether it helps them with their biggest struggle, establishing a sustainable cleaning routine, they’re unlikely to commit.

(3) the task organizer is very helpful. All your tasks cost 1-3 points (1 is easy 3 is hard) and the task organizer adds up how many pints you need each day to stay clean (ex: you might have dishes daily for one point and vacuum the living room twice weekly for 2 points for a total of 11 points per week). It then lets you set go many points you want to try to earn each day and gives you a mix of easy and hard tasks to get done. 
(4) if you do extra, you can still easily mark it. 
(5) you can divvy up the chores and workload among people and you can see which tasks were done by who and when. The app also will divvy up daily chores among different people in the group and try to rotate who does what chores so it’s not the same people all the time.

reviews.title: My family is cleaning!
reviews.text: As a family of neurodivergent people, it is often hard to get everyone to buy in to doing the mundane tasks that make our home a better place to be.  We’ve tried many checklists, chore charts, etc. The gamification aspect has really helped my family bring their A game to getting stuff done and I really find that the way the app labels rooms as clean, dirty or good enough, really does correspond to how I am experiencing those spaces IRL.  It also helps with my own all or nothing tendencies. It’s impossible to have everything be perfect all the time.  Good enough as one of the labels helps me not obsess about it.  The app does take a while to set up as you create your rooms and task lists. Don’t let that make you give up.  Just do it a little at a time. Start with one room or the most important tasks in each room and build out from there over a period of time. The premium version is very reasonable and gives you the ability to assign certain tasks to certain people and prioritize certain tasks.

reviews.title: The cycle
reviews.text:
I was overwhelmed with how messy the house was but didn’t know where to begin because it was overwhelming, which caught me in the cycle between overwhelmed, couldn’t start, and things kept getting worse. 

I made a 30 day commitment to myself and bought the upgraded version to help (so as not to “waste money.”) I started in summer, so I added my kids and paid them by their effort points.

I didn’t let myself get caught up in perfecting setting up the tasks in each room. I pretty much just used the default, and figured I could delete/add as I went.

I am now over 200 days in, and within a couple of weeks of sticking to the schedule I had set up, I started to see a difference, which motivated me to continue. In the beginning, I didn’t force everything to be perfect the first time I hit the task because I knew it would come again soon and I could concentrate on a different area.

I am now at the point where most tasks are so easy because they don’t have time to get dirty. And I don’t want that to change so I am motivated to stick to the schedule.

Kind of crazy because it’s just a house cleaning app, but I would consider this life changing.

reviews.title: Love it but I use it differently
reviews.text: I love this app! But I will say, I don’t use it as it’s designed. For me, I don’t need or want to list out tasks by room. So instead of “rooms,” I create “frequencies.” I have a “room” for daily tasks, one for every day of the week, one for monthly tasks, and one for “other.” In each “room,” I list my to-do’s, like “clean bathroom,” “dust,” etc. I don’t need to list out what I need to do in order to clean the bathroom because I know what needs to be done. I set the frequency to match the room, so daily tasks obviously are to be done every day, then the tasks in the days of the week are set to be done weekly, monthly is monthly, and “other” contains ones that are anything outside of that. For example, I have one in there for replacing my toothbrush head every 3 months, changing my furnace filters, etc. I get a very accomplished feeling when I can check off all items for the day. It’s also easier to see all at once what I want to accomplish that day. It’s easy to move things around to different days, which I did a lot at first as I was figuring out a good rhythm. I think this setup would be a great option to consider integrating as I can’t imagine I’m the only one who prefers it like this.

reviews.title: Works for dog training schedules too!

When I first tried this app, I immediately thought of the challenges of training my dog in AKC obedience. So may exercises for them to learn and so many pieces. Some things take daily work, others review at a lessor schedule. And having to come up with a plan every day and week on what we need to work on can be overwhelming. I paid for the subscription service and so far it is working great for me. I have the flexibility to add and remove things to the schedule but it also quickly finds those things I have overlooked for too long that need attention. On any given day when I don’t know what to work on, I only need to open the app. It has made our dog training sessions more organized and I add / remove items as needed. 

Since this is not the main use for this app, I have had to make a few tweaks. Every task I set up is CUSTOM and instead of room, I use general training categories such as Jumping, Essentials, Handler Training. I can also set up certain days off and change the intensity of my training days based on the apps settings. It works so well for my dog training, I bet it would also work well for cleaning my house but hey - priorities, right?

reviews.title: Sweepy has changed my life!
reviews.text:
Thou shall know firstly that I don’t review apps ever. But I can’t help lunge out of the woodwork to profess my love for this game-changer of an app.

What are my favorite aspects of Sweepy, in my first two weeks as a (heavy) user?

Sweepy is very smoothly designed, both aesthetically & sonically pleasing. One of my favorite feature is the ability to turn on/off some or all of the gamification features. As a minimalist, I love that … and I do leave a few on. I think it’d be amazing to be able to hide the Family features as well to further clean it up for the solo users—if you’re listening, developers!

Secondly, the UI is thoroughly thought out, you can sense the research and iteration behind the current version of the utility. Little bells and whistles here and there to assist you to customize your workflow—but never too heavy-handed.

In two short weeks, I’ve gone from being a slob—who couldn’t understand the lives of people with clean homes—to a super tidy-and-clean person myself. AND I’ve had fun doing it. If you consistently struggle remember and execute tasks, or if doing so seems too cognitively expensive and/or utterly joyless, do yourself a grand favor, and give this thing a chance for a month.

reviews.title: Exactly what I was looking for
reviews.text:
I’m really relieved I found this, I rely pretty heavily on it now that I’ve been using it for a few weeks. It’s too overwhelming for me to keep up with it all, but this app takes all of the thinking and remembering out of the chores and keeps me consistent. I needed an app that would keep track of how often each individual cleaning task needed to be done (because there are a million), send me notifications, and make it satisfying. 

This app lets me set all the details myself, but also gives me the option to go with its suggestions. I wanted an app that would let me have an unlimited number of customizable tasks, send me general notification reminders maybe once a day instead of overwhelming with all the specifics a thousand times a day, and give me that dopamine boost when I complete a chore. 

It organizes every chore by room, has a red to green bar for each task to visually understand how long it’s been dirty, and every time I do a chore I get coins depending on how difficult it was to finish. With the coins I get to buy furniture to decorate each room of the house, so the longer you use the app the prettier your digital home becomes. 

I think that’s brilliant, it’s an effective reward system without being too addictive or underwhelming. I love the simple bell sound that plays when I check something off, I want all my rooms to have green bars, I want cute furniture, but the game doesn’t feel too much like the main focus, it’s just a nice side effect to keeping your real life in order.

reviews.title: A fantastic app that I hope continues to grow!
reviews.text:
I love Sweepy and it has absolutely become a crucial part of my cleaning and care routine! Sweepy helps me with two main things- keeping track of the last time I completed a cleaning or care task, and motivating me to complete those tasks. I use this app every day and I love it! That being said, there is room for improvement, and I hope this app keeps getting better and better.

I am so motivated by earning coins to buy furniture for my virtual house, but I wish there was a way to see all furniture available in the game. To clarify, I love that only a few items are available for purchase each day, and that the assortment changes each morning- it makes me want to run around getting things done when I see a special item in the store! However, I would really enjoy being able to see all the items (and the colors they come in) that *might* pop into the store so that I can choose favorite items to save up for. Perhaps there could even be a wishlist feature, and notifications for when a “wished for” item was on sale in the store, prompting users to open their app and get things done.

Another change I would like to see would be a way to see my whole house and rooms without having to click on them individually. As mentioned, collecting coins for furniture really works to motivate me, but it’s a bummer that the rooms are only visible when clicking on your to do lists. I would love if there was a dollhouse-style layout wherein I could click on the individual rooms to be transported to them and their tasks, making beautifying the virtual home more important as I’d see it right when I logged on. I’d also enjoy a bit more freedom when it came to using my furniture. For instance, Why can I only have one toy in the child’s room? Why can’t I put a plant in the bathroom? If I’m not using the default living room floor, why can’t I use it in my bedroom? Why do some items display as different sizes depending on where they are placed?

Maybe this is a premium feature, but I would really like to see the history of a task. Knowing the last time I completed a task is very helpful to me, but for some tasks, I need to keep track of more than just the most recent date it was completed. I’ve been using the very helpful “note” feature to just write down the last date before it is replaced by the “new” last date, but I worry that if I forget to do so, I cannot keep track of the history. Similarly, I am disappointed that there is no way to turn an “on demand” task into a recurring task. I can edit everything about the task, but I cannot add a recurring time period to a task that did not initially have one. Because of this, I’ve had to delete and re-add a few tasks that I had initially added as “on demand” when they felt too difficult to keep up with regularly, then wanted to make them recurring once I was ready for the challenge. 

Lastly, I’d like to mention that as someone with ADHD who has trouble keeping up with a wide variety of repetitive care tasks that aren’t just cleaning related, I have several “rooms” in my “house” that are actually related to things like health, hygiene, or pets. Because Sweepy enables me to name each room whatever I want to, I am able to easily keep track of what tasks are where, even if it was not the virtual room’s intended purpose. Plus, it allows me, an apartment dweller with roommates, to decorate rooms I would not have otherwise had in my “house.” To name a few examples, I use the “Child’s Room” for tasks related to the care of my cat, the “Dressing Room” for beauty tasks like dyeing my hair or tracking my weight, and the “Office” for administrative tasks. With the ability to fully customize room names and task names and the large variety of available room types, I am perfectly content to use my virtual house in this way, but I felt I should mention it in case you are ever looking for ways to expand the game. Users could save coins to buy favorite food items to display in a “fridge” where tasks related to grocery shopping and food prep are kept, or animals, pet toys,  and pet beds could be purchased to display in a pet-care-centric area such as a Catio, Doghouse, or Stable.

Thanks for a great app!

reviews.title: Wonderful App, But Cloud Use A Little Boost In Appeal
reviews.text:
First of all, I absolutely love this app! 
It is, conceptually, exactly what I was looking for! 

Unfortunately, I feel it doesn’t quite deliver in a way that keeps my ADHD brain (or the brains of my neurodiverse kiddos) engaged. 
(I should note here that I am also physically disabled, and standing for any period of time, let alone cleaning, is challenging some days. Which makes this app both extra helpful, and at times extra frustrating). 

It is just a little unbalanced for one. The most you can get for a task, no matter how laborious or gross, is 3 coins. 
Items that come through the store often cost 30-65 coins. Nothing costs less than 5. 
Sometimes cleaning takes me literal days to recover from. So there are days I will clean until my body physically can’t do on anymore (or anything else for the next few days), and realizing I’ve only earned less than half the cost of a refrigerator. 
Even if I write down every last minor detail of the cleaning and set it to max difficulty/reward. 
This is not exactly inspiring. 

The store changes every day, which means you can’t really work towards a goal piece of furniture for your room either. 

The placement of furniture and wallpaper is clunky at best. Positioning is fixed to certain spots in certain rooms, which is ok, but if an item is already in use there is no indication until you try to place it in the room you are decorating. 
Then you have the option of removing it from wherever it is to place it, but there is no preview of what it would look like or way to undo that decision, meaning you have to backtrack and find where it was and put it back if you don’t like how it looks. 

Objects change size from room to room (and slot to slot) but you cannot choose to resize an item. Making many items much less versatile or attractive than they could be. 

All the rooms come with default furniture, walls, and floors, but those aren’t “real” items and can’t be moved from room to room (which if the rest wasn’t a pain wouldn’t matter, but it really does). 

The store only sells one of each item displayed each day, even for common wallpaper and floors. Meaning if you want the same flooring in multiple rooms it will take forever and some good luck. This feels very silly. 

What the game lacks most of all is a sense of reward agency. This is, in many ways, a self motivation app. 
But I can’t configure the app to be motivating for me personally, despite knowing what would help. 
Even just the ability to dole out bonus coin as a household manager would be hugely helpful. 

My kids only engaged for one day, saw there was no real reward for participating, and fell off entirely. 

I still feel like it was money well spent, just as an organized to-do list. 
And I’m trying to think of ways to compensate for the apps lack of rewards that will re-engage my kids. (Something that would really be wonderful as a chronically ill solo parent!) 

Things I love! 

1) The ability to create your house and organize tasks by room. 

2) The fact you can choose between daily, one time, and on demand tasks to assign to a space. 

3) The household management system! I love being able to add my kids, whether they have their own accounts or not! (Mine do have devices, but was impressed there was an option to add them either way!) 
I love that I was able to extend my purchase to their accounts through Apple family sharing, thank you for that! 
And I love that I can configure the wildcard system, as the default was immediately intimidating. 

4) I LOVE LOVE LOVE the streak feature! That is always such a good motivator! 
Though the reward for keeping your streak is not motivating enough to keep my kids engaged, unfortunately.

I appreciate all the hard work that has clearly been but into the very solid bones and foundation of this app!

All that I love aside, it is hard to stay engaged, and even harder to convince my kids to open the app. 
But it really doesn’t feel like it needs to be this way. It would take so little to make it so much better. 
So here are some ideas:
 
1) Let us configure our coin rewards as a part of household management. 

2) Let each household member pin an item in their personal store, so we can save towards a goal. 

3) Let all/most items go in all rooms and in all slots. What does it hurt if we put a toilet in the bedroom? It is incredibly limiting at the moment, and disappointing when you can’t put, say, a potted plant outside or some such. 

With this maybe let household management assign who can rearrange which room/lock rooms if that is not already a feature (I haven’t checked). 

4) Let us chose the size of items that come in multiple sizes. Why is this rug nice and big in the bed room, and then tiny in the dining room? Etc. 

5) Either have a store that has basic item like common walls and floors always for sale in addition to the store, or let us buy more than one wall/floor at a time. 

6) Streak rewards. It feels more like a punishment to not keep your streak than a reward to keep it, which is not ideal in an app that is already unbalanced coin to cost wise. 
Would love to see a real reward for engaging daily! I think my kids would actually use the app if that were the case! (Coin that ramps up each day? A piece of furniture on day X? Maybe a ticket for the store that can buy you anything after a month or some such?) 

If you want more people to engage with your app, the decorating aspect really needs to be improved. 
If you took it more seriously, and got it working well, you could eventually run daily login events and such with unique themed rewards. 

It’s a really great app, and has the potential to be so much better and even more popular! 

As it is, I intend to keep using it, or trying to, but I know I will fall off again most likely as it is largely an organized to-do list at the moment.

All the best, and thanks again for your hard work! I hope to see your app growing in popularity and success in the future!

reviews.title: Persistent Daily Notifications
reviews.text: This app is good for people who need aggressive daily reminders to do their chores - either because they have daily tasks, or because they need constant reminders on their phone. This didn't suit my household's needs, so we cancelled our subscription and deleted our account. (Btw, the household leader has to delete the entire house's account.) We only track weekly chores and recurring tasks 2-6 months from the last completion date. We started ignoring Sweepy's daily notifications, which defeats the purpose of using a paid app. I enabled the  “Daily reminder notification” and disabled “Plan your day reminder notification". Push notifications appeared every day, even when no tasks were due. Unfortunately, support confirmed that this design was intentional. What I enjoyed about Sweepy was its intuitive UI. You got a list view of all rooms and tasks, plus a visual calendar of your tasks for the week. The simple three-point “Effort” rating made it easy to ensure an equitable distribution of task difficulty for the household. Gamification options were individual: achievements for exploring the app, streaks for keeping up with your tasks, and coins for buying virtual house decorations. A competition mode might be good to incentivize slackers in the house.

reviews.title: The family is finally helping!
reviews.text: This app has been a game-changer!!! I tried to write my own solution in another organization tool and it required way too much maintenance work because it lacked needed features. Sweepy has all the features I was hoping for: - Assign some rooms or tasks to specific people - Adjust the frequency of tasks individually - Set some tasks to be seasonal (bring in firewood) or “on demand” (unpack from trip) - Create custom “Rooms” (we have Car and Errands, so you’re not even limited to actual Rooms) to group custom tasks together - Only positive reinforcement; no penalties! (And yet the tasks will come right back in a few days if you don’t do them the first time) - Data on whether the current assigned “Effort” will allow the household to cover all tasks configured (I’m learning to adjust my expectations) - Color-coding helps the family have a gut feel on how the household is doing as a whole - Self-reported accountability (absolutely key for tweens and teens in my opinion because they need to develop these skills for themselves, not just when Mom is watching) We are only a few days in, but my “agent of chaos” spouse and Autistic teen have both done tasks and say the app is intuitive and helpful. The daughter home from college who just had surgery is temporarily on a reduced “Effort” which she can increase as she heals and then set to 0 when she goes back to school. I’m really optimistic that this tool is going to work much better than paper chore checklists and To Do apps we’ve tried in the past!

reviews.title: Almost great, but not usable
reviews.text:
I love the idea of this app. It would definitely help my
roommate and I keep the house clean more effectively, and I’ve really enjoyed it when it works. 

Pros:
-room by room chore assignments 
-ability to invite others into household (theoretical)
-ability to set energy level and frequency for chores

Cons:
-huge interface issues. I am paying for premium, but I’m run through a login loop whenever I try to access my calendar. It keeps saying I need to create an account, but then won’t let me advance because my email is already registered. I know. I’m signed in, and I don’t want to recreate the entire chore list under a new email,

-obnoxious messaging. For years, I would get a notification saying “what smells?” To remind me to clean. It’s incredibly rude. Like many people, I downloaded this app to help build good habits. I don’t need to be begged by it.

-cutesy messaging: separating from the above because it’s awful in a different way. For example, it uses German for some reason to tell me I can’t use the email address I used to make the account. 

-poor communication: blanket term for the above two, but also, the only way to contact support through the app is to use Apple mail. Almost no one uses Apple mail. Why? 

I don’t know why the developers refuse to use standard practices. They have a great app, but these simple mistakes make the app unusable. I hope they get it together someday, because this is a great idea.

reviews.title: You Need This
reviews.text:
I don’t usually write reviews but if you’re reading this and considering whether this app will improve your life - let me tell you, it will. 

One of the trickiest parts of maintaining the space you live in (apartment, house, travel van, whatever!) is keeping track of what needs to be done/when. This app takes that mental load OFF your plate, so you can simply open the app and see the list of which things need to be done. 

I’ve been using this app a year and I use it every day. It’ll take an ~hour to build your tasks the way you prefer. If you are married, schedule a “date” to build everything as a team (use this time to discuss what chores, the frequency, etc). Whether your married or not, use Google to find inspiration for your cleaning tasks.

This app has not only kept me sane, but it’s allowed our household to delegate the mental load of “what/when” to an app. No more conversations about “how can I help” or “I didn’t know what needed to be done” or “what should I do” — it’s all in the app. The app also keeps track of who is doing what, giving visibility to the invisible labor to keep a house clean and running smoothly. 

This app has transformed not only HOW I CLEAN my house (a little bit every day - instead of a frenzied multiple hour session every weekend) but it has also transformed my house into being “a house that’s ALWAYS CLEAN”. 

Get this app: you need it.
Once you love it: treat yourself to the premium version. You deserve it.

However. In the past month there have been a ton of glitches. Tasks that were checked off reappear constantly, no reloading appropriately if you are using it linked to several devices. Seasonal tasks that aren’t for this season showing up, etc. The whole point of this app is keep track of tasks done and needing done. At this rate I won’t be renewing our yearly subscription. 

I reached out to support and they wanted pictures and videos. Not sure how practical taking a video of me ‘checking’ off a task one day and then another when it reappears 2 days later instead of 2 weeks as scheduled would help 😂 I’m currently on the look out for a different app but hoping they finally fix this one.
